topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecturer, sets the context within the cancer lecture series, and outlines the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Intrinsic 'Bad Luck' versus Environmental Factors in Cancer Risk
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the fundamental interplay between intrinsic mutational processes, inherited predisposition, and environmental exposures in driving cancer incidence.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Carcinogenic Agents and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: They investigate the diverse molecular and cellular mechanisms through which chemical, physical, and infectious agents initiate DNA damage or promote tumor growth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: They present the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to identify carcinogens and evaluate mutagenic potential.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Everyday Risk-Benefit Decisions
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with final summary remarks on environmental cancer causation and individual risk-benefit assessment.
